title: SeaweedFS S3 write probe
description: One probe object put, read back, deleted and confirmed gone in an EXISTING bucket through one S3 gateway pod, with no credentials; the task never creates or deletes a bucket. plan is what the task does (or would do, in a dry run); steps are what it did, each with ok and the error (a failed work step is also a partial-result error with scope s3-check/<step>). bucketListing: allowed (an anonymous list answered 200) or denied (401/403: a write-only anonymous identity is possible, so the write is still tried; its result is reported separately). passed is true when every step of the plan ran and succeeded and nothing is left behind, false when any work step failed (PUT, read-back, DELETE, confirmation) or the cleanup left something, null in a dry run. anonymousWrite true: an unauthenticated PUT was accepted from the pod network (the API-server proxy strips Authorization) AND the read-back matched; false: the PUT answered 2xx but the read-back differs; null: the PUT failed or the read-back did not answer. contentMatches: the object read back equals what was written. leftBehind lists bucket/object paths a failed cleanup could not remove. The API server shows no body of a non-2xx answer, so an error message is the status, not SeaweedFS's explanation.
